components.note: Durrett pp. 3-4: semialgebra, algebra generated (Lemma 1.1.7), 'measure on an algebra' (identified as premeasure, line 49), sigma-finiteness.
Durrett Lemma 1.1.7, Thm 1.1.9 first part / Thm A.1.1 and Lemma 1.1.10 (pp. 4-5, 455-456) with written proofs.
Durrett App. A.1 p. 458: outer measure, measurability criterion (A.1.1) and the sufficiency of (A.1.2).
Durrett Lemma A.1.7 with its remark that it holds for any outer measure (pp. 459-460); completeness added.

components.gap: The cover formula is Durrett's (App. A.1 p. 458). Not supplied: his justification of it (p. 458), that any measure nu agreeing with mu on the algebra satisfies nu(E) <= sum nu(A_i) = sum mu(A_i) for every cover, so mu*(E) is an upper bound for the measure of E, and that 'the measurable sets are the ones for which the upper bound is tight'. Neither the justification nor the upper-bound property of mu* for every extension is stated on the input route.

components.note: Durrett Thm A.1.3 (existence without sigma-finiteness, uniqueness under it), Lemma A.1.6, and Thm 1.1.9's sigma-finite clause (pp. 5, 456-459).

components.gap: Durrett's Stieltjes measure function (Ex. 1.1.3, p. 3) and the endpoint values (p. 5) are covered. Not supplied: the source's justification of the half-open convention (p. 3), that 'closed on the right' is dictated by the intersection of (a,b_n] over n being (a,b] when b_n decreases to b (matching right continuity), and that 'open on the left' is explained by the semialgebra complement property. The definition adopts (a,b] without this justification; the annex verifies the semialgebra property (lines 276-286) without connecting either fact to the choice of endpoints.

components.note: Durrett Thm 1.1.4 (p. 3) and its proof (pp. 5-6): endpoint limits, finite partition condition, compactness argument, unbounded targets, uniqueness.
Durrett p. 3 (F(x) = x gives Lebesgue measure) and the uniform space of Thm 1.2.2 (p. 11).
Worked boundary for the sigma-finiteness clause of Durrett Thms 1.1.9/A.1.3; both extensions verified countably additive and different on singletons.
Durrett Thm 1.2.2's X(w) = sup{y: F(y) < w} (p. 11), identified as his generalized inverse.

components.gap: Durrett Thm 1.2.2 is covered and extended (ray equivalence, fibers, flat portions). Not supplied: the remark after it (p. 11) calling the construction the inverse F^{-1} and stating that it is how random variables are generated on a computer, a uniform U being transformed into F^{-1}(U) with distribution function F; the theorem realizes the law only by Q_F on the constructed uniform space, and the statement for a uniform variable on an arbitrary probability space and its computational use are not on the input route. In addition, the annex (lines 512-516) obtains equality of the law of Q_F with mu_F and uniqueness 'among all Borel probability laws' by citing thm:p15-cdf-laws, which is stated for laws of real random variables; the step exhibiting a Borel probability measure as such a law (or a direct appeal to the pi-system uniqueness theorem) is not written.

components.note: Handbook example; quantile values, masses and the u = F(2-) boundary verified.
Worked boundary for the right-continuity and open-interval hypotheses of Thm 1.2.2; verified.
Pointer to secs 1.4-1.6 resolves to the next chapter on the route; the multidimensional Stieltjes construction lies outside this unit's cited theorems and is stated as not established here.
